readback.name: Poincare.heatKernel_fourier_complex_eq_ofReal
readback.mathematical_statement: Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its compatible normed additive group structure, in an arbitrary universe u_1. Put n = finrank_R E and H_t(z) = (4*pi*t)^(-n/2) * exp(-||z||^2/(4*t)), with real power and real exponential as in the pinned heatKernel definition. For every real t > 0 and every x,y in E, put c = ((4*pi^2)*t)^(-1), computed in R. Then ((pi:C)*(c:C))^((n:C)/2) * Complex.exp(-(pi:C)^2*(c:C)*(||x-y||:C)^2) = (H_t(x-y):C). The normalization power on the left is complex cpow with complex exponent n/2, whereas the squared norm uses natural-number power 2. Every displayed real quantity is embedded into C by ofReal where the frozen type specifies it. Since t > 0, c and pi*c are positive real numbers, so the principal complex logarithm gives the same real power normalization and no branch ambiguity occurs. The identity is pointwise and has no measurable-space, measure, integral, Fourier-transform, orientation, or continuity hypothesis or conclusion. The dimension may be any natural number, including zero; it is not fixed to three. No assertion is made at t = 0 or at negative time. E alone has the universe parameter u_1; the scalar fields R and C are in universe zero. This identifies two Gaussian formulas and by itself asserts neither a heat-equation solution nor a topological result.

readback.name: Poincare.heatSolution_apply_swap
readback.mathematical_statement: Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its compatible normed additive group structure, in any universe u_1, equipped with a measurable structure that is its Borel sigma-algebra. The volume in the frozen type is the canonical inner-product Lebesgue, or additive Haar, measure obtained from the standard orthonormal basis; an orthonormal parallelepiped has measure one. No arbitrary MeasureSpace argument or rescaled Haar measure is quantified, and no orientation is assumed. For every real t, every function f:E->R, and every x in E, heatSolution t f x = integral over y in E of H_t(x-y)*f(y) against this volume, where H_t is the pinned real Gaussian (4*pi*t)^(-n/2)*exp(-||z||^2/(4*t)) and n = finrank_R E. The pinned heatSolution is defined instead as integral over y of H_t(y)*f(x-y), through real scalar multiplication convolution. The displayed equality changes variables by the measure-preserving involution y -> x-y. Reflection and translation preserve this positive volume measure in every dimension, without an oriented sign. Both sides are real Bochner integrals in Lean, whose value is defined to be zero for a nonintegrable integrand. Thus this equality requires neither t > 0 nor measurability, integrability, continuity, boundedness, or compact support of f, and does not assert that the integrand is integrable. The Gaussian formula is a total Lean function also at zero and negative time; this identity does not give those times the positive-time fundamental-solution interpretation. E is universe-polymorphic with parameter u_1 and the real output is in universe zero. The dimension includes zero. This is an equality of two convolution formulas, with no convergence or PDE claim.

readback.name: Poincare.tendsto_heatSolution_nhdsGT_zero
readback.mathematical_statement: For any finite-dimensional real inner-product space E with its compatible normed additive group structure in any universe u_1 and its Borel measurable structure, fix a real-valued function f:E->R integrable against the canonical inner-product volume measure. Integrable here supplies almost-everywhere strong measurability and finite integral of the norm, equivalently absolute integrability for this real codomain. At any x in E where f is continuous, heatSolution t f x tends to the actual real value f(x) as real t tends to zero through strictly positive values. Precisely, the source filter is nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0), the right-hand neighborhood filter at zero, and the target filter is the ordinary real neighborhood filter nhds (f x). With n = finrank_R E and H_t(z) = (4*pi*t)^(-n/2)*exp(-||z||^2/(4*t)), the heatSolution definition is real scalar multiplication convolution against canonical volume, integral of H_t(y)*f(x-y), equivalently integral of H_t(x-y)*f(y) by the preceding formula. The measure is the orthonormal-basis normalized Lebesgue, or additive Haar, measure, independent of orientation; there is no arbitrary or weighted measure argument. Continuity is assumed only at the selected x and global integrability is assumed for f. No global continuity, boundedness, compact support, or positive dimension hypothesis appears. The statement includes dimension zero and arbitrary universe u_1 for E, with R in universe zero. It asserts recovery at a continuity point as t -> 0+, and does not specify a value of heatSolution at zero, a limit from negative time, convergence uniformly in x, convergence in an Lp norm, a convergence rate, spatial or temporal differentiability, or satisfaction of a PDE. It is a model-space approximate-identity statement and makes no manifold or Poincare-conjecture claim.
